title: Sustainable biodegradable P34HB/rGO composite membranes for direct borohydride fuel cells with enhanced electrochemical performance
content: Biodegradable polymer-based membranes are of interest as potential alternatives to conventional perfluorinated membranes for fuel cell applications. In this study, reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-reinforced poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-4-hydroxybutyrate) (P34HB) composite membranes were evaluated as electrolyte membranes for direct borohydride fuel cells (DBFCs). Membranes containing 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt% rGO were investigated at operating temperatures of 25 and 60 °C and fuel flow rates of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 mL min−1. The effects of membrane composition and operating conditions on cell performance were systematically assessed. Among the tested compositions and operating conditions, the 5 wt% rGO membrane achieved the highest power density of 27 mW cm−2 at 60 °C and a fuel flow rate of 1.0 mL min−1. Performance varied with fuel flow rate, with 1.0 mL min−1 providing the highest power density for the 5 wt% rGO membrane at 60 °C. Previous characterization of these membranes showed that increasing rGO content enhanced proton conductivity and water uptake while reducing tensile strength, highlighting the importance of considering electrochemical and mechanical properties together in membrane development. Unlike our previous study, which investigated P34HB/rGO membranes in microbial fuel cells, the present work evaluates their performance in DBFCs under different operating conditions. These findings demonstrate the potential of biodegradable P34HB/rGO composite membranes for DBFC applications and provide a basis for further optimization of membrane composition and operating conditions.
